feature.summary: How the AGI Mobile app moves between chats, lists and settings. Phones get a slide-out drawer plus stack pages with back gestures. Windows 1000 points wide or more get a permanent side panel. Camera, scan and voice pages hide the drawer. Phones stay in portrait. Tablets may rotate. Mobile only.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives the Mobile app its frame. A drawer holds the Local/Cloud mode switch, search, new chat, destinations (projects, library, images, schedules and others), recent chats, settings. Stack pages open on top. The layout changes with the window width, and the screen orientation is locked for phones.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief asks for native patterns: a swipeable drawer plus stack routes with back gestures (S71.01), a wider tablet layout that adapts to split view (S71.25), foldable adaptation (S71.26) and landscape adaptation (S71.27). (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/071-mobile-application.md)
purpose.who_uses_it: Every person who uses AGI Mobile on a phone or tablet, in Local mode or Cloud mode.
problems_solved: Reach chats and tools with one thumb on a phone.
Use the room on a tablet instead of a stretched phone layout.
Stop the drawer swipe from fighting the Back swipe on settings pages or the voice screen.
Keep the camera and voice pages full screen.
use_cases: Swipe from the left edge on a phone, then tap a recent chat to open it.
Open Settings and swipe from the left edge to go Back.
Use a large iPad window where the drawer stays open beside the chat.
Watch a video full screen in landscape on a phone, then return to portrait.

where_to_find_it: Mobile: the whole app shell. The menu control is the round button with accessibility label 'Open navigation drawer' (apps/mobile/src/shared/components/DrawerButton.tsx:70-95).

Mobile drawer rows: Search, 'New chat', destination rows, Recents, 'See all chats', Settings (keys drawer.newChat, search, drawer.recents, drawer.seeAllChats, settings) (apps/mobile/src/features/drawer/components/DrawerContent.tsx:631-912).
Web, Desktop, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: not part of this feature (brief gives a status for the mobile app only).
prerequisites: None for Local mode. The drawer lists only rows allowed in the current mode (isShownInMode) and by feature flags (apps/mobile/src/features/drawer/components/DrawerContent.tsx:563-573).
Some rows need Cloud mode, a signed-in account, or a plan capability (Images, AGI Work tasks) (DrawerContent.tsx:337-345, 563-573).
screens_and_controls: Drawer (overlay on narrow windows, permanent panel on wide ones) with a Local/Cloud mode switch, Search, New chat, a 'More' fold, Projects, Recents list with long-press actions, 'See all chats', Settings and (only where native purchases exist) an Upgrade row (DrawerContent.tsx:323-420, 631-912).
Menu button with an unread-notification pip; on a permanent sidebar it becomes a blank slot and shows only a pip link 'Open notifications, N unread' (DrawerButton.tsx:50-95).
Settings stack: Back by edge swipe or back control.
Camera and scan pages: full window, no drawer.
Voice page: always dark, drawer swipe off.
journey: Open the app. On a phone the chat shows with the drawer closed.
Swipe from the left edge (40 points on iOS, 64 on Android, drag of at least 60 on iOS or 96 on Android) or tap the menu button.
Tap a chat, a destination or Settings. The drawer closes and the page opens.
In Settings, swipe from the left edge or tap Back to return one page.
On a window 1000 points wide or more, the drawer is already open at 280 points wide and the menu button is gone.
Rotate an iPhone or an Android phone: the screen stays portrait, except while a video or a presentation viewer is open.
feedback_and_outputs: The drawer slides over the page with a scrim (apps/mobile/app/(app)/_layout.tsx:55-70).
The active chat row is highlighted and unread chats show a dot (DrawerContent.tsx:500-560).
Unread count shows on the menu button and is read out in its label (DrawerButton.tsx:77-84).
settings: Chat list arrangement: 'In one list' or 'By project' (drawer.inOneList, drawer.byProject) stored in the settings store (DrawerContent.tsx:358-380).
The 'More' fold and the folded Projects section remember their state (DrawerContent.tsx:352-357).

working: Drawer type is 'front' (overlay) on narrow windows and 'permanent' when the window is 1000 points wide or more (280 drawer + 720 content) (apps/mobile/src/shared/hooks/useResponsiveLayout.ts:3-9, 24-47; apps/mobile/src/features/shell/drawerGestures.ts:23-45).
The draft's 768 and 1024 are not the drawer switch. 768 sets the 'tablet' size class and 1024 (largest side of the screen) sets isTablet (apps/mobile/src/shared/hooks/useTabletLayout.ts:5-6, 40-50).
Split view is detected as a window narrower than the screen by at least 8 points on a tablet-size screen (useTabletLayout.ts:9, 51).
Settings pages turn the drawer swipe off so the edge swipe means Back (apps/mobile/app/(app)/_layout.tsx:20-22, 122).
Camera and scan are drawerType 'front' even where a sidebar is permanent. The voice route also turns swipe off (_layout.tsx:23-28, 130-134).
A leftover open state is closed when the window grows to the permanent width (_layout.tsx:30-41).

Phones are locked to portrait at app start by lockPhonePortrait (apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:122, 129; apps/mobile/src/shared/hooks/useLandscapeWhileOpen.ts:23-25). A phone is any non-iPad iOS device or an Android device whose smaller side is under 600 dp (useLandscapeWhileOpen.ts:11-16).

Only the video player and the presentation deck viewer free rotation while open (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/VideoPlayerModal.tsx:47; apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/artifact-viewers/presentation/PresentationDeckView.tsx:161).

iPad lists all four orientations and multitasking is on (supportsTablet true, requireFullScreen false) (apps/mobile/app.config.js:156-186). A native Android plugin lets screens with smallest width 600 dp or more rotate and re-decides when the size changes (apps/mobile/native/android/withAGITabletOrientation.cjs:14-34).

Message list and composer keep a reading column up to 720 points wide on large windows (apps/mobile/src/shared/layout/contentColumn.ts:3-25; apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageList.tsx:367-370).
incomplete: Landscape on phones: the brief wants the chat re-laid out in landscape (S71.27) but the code locks phones to portrait. Only two viewers rotate. (apps/mobile/app.config.js:158; useLandscapeWhileOpen.ts:23-52)

Foldables: only window-size changes are handled, through the Android orientation plugin and the width-based layout. No hinge or fold event code was found. (apps/mobile/native/android/withAGITabletOrientation.cjs; search for fold/hinge in apps/mobile returned only a test case name)
disconnected_or_disabled: The Upgrade row in the drawer appears only when native purchases are available. Billing is off in the feature flags, so it is hidden in the current build. (DrawerContent.tsx:337-345; apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:6)
Companion pages are registered as drawer screens but FEATURES.companion is false. (apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:16; _layout.tsx:110-114)
not_available: Web, Desktop, CLI, VS Code and Chrome: not applicable to this feature.

established.statement: The phone app navigates with native patterns: a swipeable drawer plus stack routes with back gestures.
On tablets the app uses a wider layout (persistent drawer, multi-column grids) and adapts to split view.
On foldables the layout adapts when the device folds or unfolds, ideally around the hinge. The brief status is not applicable anywhere.
Rotating the phone to landscape re-lays out the chat usefully.
The design contract names breakpoints: compact phone, phone, tablet, narrow desktop, desktop, wide desktop.

acceptance_criteria: On a phone, a swipe from the left edge opens the drawer and a tap on a recent chat opens it and closes the drawer.
On Settings pages the edge swipe goes Back and does not open the drawer.
With a window 1000 points wide or more the drawer is permanent and the menu button is not shown. Narrowing the window below 1000 closes any stale open state and the overlay drawer works.
Opening camera, scan or voice shows no drawer. Voice does not react to an edge swipe.
An iPhone and a small Android phone stay in portrait when turned; an iPad and an Android tablet rotate.
Opening a video or a presentation on a phone allows landscape and closing it returns to portrait.
inferred: The brief status 'done' for S71.27 conflicts with the portrait lock, so the status is either stale or means tablets only. [inferred]
A tablet in portrait between 768 and 999 points gets the overlay drawer, not a permanent one. [inferred from useResponsiveLayout.ts:24-47]
proposed: [proposed] Decide and record whether phone landscape is a product requirement. If yes, unlock rotation for the chat and re-lay out the composer. If no, change S71.27 to match the code.
[proposed] Add a posture or hinge signal for foldables only if a target device needs it.

steps.what_happens: The app reads window and screen size and chooses overlay or permanent drawer.
A swipe or a tap on the menu opens the drawer; a row tap calls router.navigate and closes the drawer.
At start the root layout locks a phone to portrait through expo-screen-orientation.
Drawer rows read conversations and projects from device stores; Cloud rows come from the Cloud message store that a sync loop fills.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: None. Navigation does not call a model or provider. The drawer filters conversations by their execution mode so Local and Cloud lists stay separate (DrawerContent.tsx:481-490).

access_and_usage.account: No account is needed to use the shell in Local mode. Cloud destinations and the Cloud mode switch need a signed-in account (DrawerContent.tsx:337-345).
access_and_usage.subscription: Images and AGI Work task rows depend on the plan capability documents (DrawerContent.tsx:337-345, 563-568). Drawer itself has no plan rule.
access_and_usage.flags: FEATURES.schedules, research, cloudTasks and billing change which rows show (DrawerContent.tsx:563-568; apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts).
access_and_usage.local_mode: The shell works fully in Local mode with no sign-in. Rows that are Cloud-only are hidden by isShownInMode (DrawerContent.tsx:568).

corrections.claim: 768 sets the 'tablet' size class and 1024 (largest screen side) sets isTablet
corrections.what_the_code_shows: 768 sets sizeClass 'tablet' from window width, but 1024 also sets sizeClass 'regular' from window width. isTablet uses the largest screen side >= 1024. Split view is window width <= screen width - 8 on a tablet screen.
corrections.correction: 768 gives size class 'tablet' and window width 1024 or more gives 'regular'. isTablet is true when the screen's larger side is 1024 or more.

corrections.claim: The Upgrade row appears only when native purchases are available; billing is off in the feature flags so it is hidden (DrawerContent.tsx:337-345; v1FeatureFlags.ts:6)
corrections.what_the_code_shows: showUpgrade is gated by NATIVE_PURCHASES_AVAILABLE (read from storePurchases.json), Cloud mode, a signed-in Clerk user and a free plan tier. It does not read FEATURES.billing. The cited lines 337-345 are the AGI Work gate; showUpgrade is at 396-402.
corrections.correction: The Upgrade row shows only in Cloud mode, signed in, on a free plan, and when storePurchases.json sets nativePurchases true. FEATURES.billing is not part of that check, and the page does not say what the JSON value is.

corrections.claim: Feature flags: FEATURES.schedules, research, cloudTasks and billing change which rows show (DrawerContent.tsx:563-568)
corrections.what_the_code_shows: The row filter uses schedules, research and cloudTasks (plus showImages and showAgiWork). billing is not used there. Also FEATURES.projects gates the project list at line 452.
corrections.correction: FEATURES.schedules, research and cloudTasks (and projects for the projects section) change which rows show. billing does not; the Upgrade row follows NATIVE_PURCHASES_AVAILABLE.

corrections.claim: Account: Cloud destinations and the Cloud mode switch need a signed-in account (DrawerContent.tsx:337-345)
corrections.what_the_code_shows: Lines 337-345 only gate the AGI Work row (Cloud mode, plan capability, granted canUseAgiWork). The Images row needs Cloud mode plus a Clerk sign-in (347-349). The mode switch uses cloudUnlocked from useAppModeSwitch (333, 637); the page did not read that hook, so the sign-in claim for the switch is not shown by the cited lines.
corrections.correction: The Images row needs Cloud mode and a signed-in account. The AGI Work row needs Cloud mode, the plan and the granted capability. Whether the Cloud switch needs sign-in is decided by cloudUnlocked in useAppModeSwitch, which the page does not trace.

corrections.claim: Drawer rows read conversations from device stores; Cloud rows come from the Cloud message store a sync loop fills; list filtered by execution mode
corrections.what_the_code_shows: In Cloud mode the list is the cloud conversation store (cloudConversations), in Local mode the local store, then filtered by executionModeForConversation === appMode. The cited lines are 446-455, not 481-496 (that range is the pinned/recent slicing). Code comment says the local store holds a stale mirror for Cloud rows. Recents are capped by DRAWER_RECENT_LIMIT.
corrections.correction: Cited lines should be 446-455. The source store is chosen by mode and then filtered by execution mode; recents are capped by DRAWER_RECENT_LIMIT (the page does not say so).

missing_facts: The Upgrade row also needs a free plan tier, Cloud mode and a signed-in Clerk user, and its on/off switch is storePurchases.json nativePurchases (apps/mobile/src/features/billing/nativePurchaseAvailability.ts:3; DrawerContent.tsx:396-402), not FEATURES.billing.

The drawer shows only DRAWER_RECENT_LIMIT recent chats (pinned first) and at most 6 projects in Cloud mode (apps/mobile/src/features/drawer/components/DrawerContent.tsx:446-470, 481-493). The page's Limits row says none found.

Camera and scan keep the swipe-open overlay drawer on phones; only voice disables the swipe (apps/mobile/app/(app)/_layout.tsx:25-28). The page's 'Camera, scan and voice pages hide the drawer' overstates this.
